rules.coverage_note: The manifest states the dependency; the resolved version and the enabled feature set are Cargo's, not the overlay's.

omega-rust names an attribute by the last segment of its path, so #[tokio::main] and a bare #[main] are the same fact; the crate's tokio dependency is what separates them. #[tokio::test] is indistinguishable from #[test] and is deliberately not matched.
An import is named by the last segment of its path, so use std::sync::mpsc and use tokio::sync::mpsc are the same fact; the crate's tokio dependency is the only separation available.
The Task is the authored spawn site. Scheduling, JoinHandle identity and completion are runtime state and are not claimed.
set.spawn(..) on a JoinSet and handle.spawn(..) on a Handle. omega-rust names a method call by its member alone, so a std::process::Command::spawn in a tokio crate matches here too.
Where the runtime is configured. Runtime::new() is not matched: its member is the bare new.
Where synchronous code enters the runtime.
The flavour (mpsc / oneshot / broadcast / watch) is the dropped qualifier of the call path; tokio.facility.import carries it per file.
Which functions wait on the clock or bound a future in time.
Which function listens for the shutdown signal. ctrl_c is a name tokio alone uses.
select!, join! and try_join! are also spelled by the futures crate; the crate's tokio dependency is the only separation available.
Which functions declare or return a task handle -- the signature-level answer to which functions hand a task back to their caller.
Mutex, RwLock and Sender are also std spellings; in a crate that depends on tokio the type mention is reported without claiming which module it came from.
Which functions handle a socket. The same names exist in std::net; the qualifier is not published by omega-rust.

gaps: omega-rust names a scoped call, a scoped attribute and a use path by its last segment only, so tokio::spawn and any other spawn are one fact; every rule here is gated on the crate's Cargo.toml tokio dependency and claims no more than that
authored spawn/select/channel/timer/network sites are materialized; scheduling, wakeups, task completion and actual resource use remain runtime state
#[tokio::main] is declaration evidence only and is never expanded; #[tokio::test] is not matched at all because it is indistinguishable from #[test]
